comparator.name: International Development Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official handbook defines 180 EC: 114 EC of common study, a 36-EC specialisation and 30 EC of open electives. Sociology of Development is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break from the three equally formal specialisations.
components: Global Challenges and Communication in a Changing World
Research Methods in the Social Sciences
Critical Perspectives on Agricultural and Rural Development
Economics Evolving: A History of Ideas of Development and Growth
Economic and Sociological Analysis of Rural Livelihoods
Methods, Techniques and Data Analysis for Field Research
Globalization and Sustainability of Food Production and Consumption
The Sociology of Farming and Rural Life
Planetary Development: Sociological and Anthropological Perspectives
Genuine open elective space; no minor or course package is invented.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target has three equally formal 36-EC specialisations: Sociology of Development, Economics of Development, and Politics and Communication in Development. None is identified as the general route, so the first current handbook specialisation is selected neutrally and independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: International development, inequality & governance
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines sociology, political science, economics, international law, history, communication and mixed research methods around inequality, justice and global development.
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible international-development programme combining sociology, economics, politics, law, history and research methods to examine inequality, livelihoods, institutions, justice and global change.
alternatives.distinctness: Thirteen courses differ in each direction from CHS and twenty from Earth and Sustainability. Political economy, legal institutions, human rights and international security become the organising core.
progression: Sociology, politics, economics, law, history and methods foundations precede international law, public economics, econometrics, institutions and advanced global-governance study. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Development economics & global political economy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres macroeconomics, microeconomics, public and behavioural economics, econometrics and quantitative methods alongside politics, law and global institutions.
alternatives.concept: Develops the official Economics of Development direction through economic theory, econometrics, political economy, international institutions, law and policy analysis.
progression: Political, economic, mathematical and research foundations precede macroeconomics, microeconomics, public economics, econometrics, behavioural economics and advanced governance study. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; six 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes development economics, quantitative evidence and political economy the organising priority. It differs from the closest programme by six courses and 45 EC.

alternatives.label: Development sociology, culture & communication
alternatives.concept: Combines the official Sociology of Development and Politics and Communication directions through sociology, culture, inequality, history, media, rhetoric, justice and qualitative inquiry.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres sociology, culture, history, inequality, environmental justice, media, communication and qualitative research.
progression: Sociology, politics, history, ethics, law and qualitative-method foundations precede advanced social theory, global histories, media, race, documentary and communication. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes development sociology, culture and communication the organising priority. It differs from the closest programme by thirteen courses and from the economics direction by fifteen courses.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: International development, inequality, poverty and livelihoods
Development economics, political economy and resource distribution
Politics, governance, international institutions, law and justice
Communication, social change, culture and participation
Statistics, qualitative and quantitative field research, policy analysis and thesis work
adjacent: Development economics and global political economy
Environment, food systems and sustainable development
questions: Why are wealth, food security and opportunities distributed unequally?
How can institutions, rights, communication and participation support fairer development?
How do economic and environmental policies reshape livelihoods and sustainability?

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates inequality, economics, politics, law and methods. The official Economics of Development and combined Sociology of Development/Politics and Communication directions support two further coherent, feasible and pairwise-distinct alternatives. Production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: WUR provides a dedicated development-studies sequence with rural livelihoods, agricultural development, specialised field research and a development thesis. UCR can combine substantial sociology, economics, politics, law, history and communication, but does not reproduce the same field-based or rural-development sequence course for course.
